items.title: #NSTviral: Redang coral reefs deteriorating amid overtourism, poor awareness [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Coral reefs around Pulau Redang are showing signs of continued deterioration, with increasing tourist activity, anchoring practices and low awareness among some visitors placing added pressure on the island's marine ecosystem. The data, collected after the Covid-19 pandemic in 2021, indicated that the condition of coral reefs around Redang had continued to decline year by year. The video said this could damage coral reefs, including areas undergoing restoration.

items.title: OGA 2026 brings oil, gas and energy players under one roof
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Oil & Gas Asia (OGA) 2026 returns to provide a platform for players in the oil and gas industry — including policymakers, energy companies, engineering firms and investors — to connect and collaborate. "Petronas works alongside partners across the value chain to deliver energy safely, reliably and sustainably while advancing energy transition. "OGA brings together key energy industry players under one roof, creating meaningful opportunities for collaboration, innovation and business growth.

items.title: Muzz, Coffee Meets Bagel step up safeguards as romance scams evolve
items.summary: Muslim dating and marriage application Muzz has made selfie verification compulsory for new members joining the platform, as part of measures to detect fake profiles and prevent banned users from returning. Muzz Asia-Pacific Region Growth lead Ary Mozta said the platform used automated and manual checks to ensure users were genuine and that their profile photos matched their verification selfies. "Beyond verification, Muzz has a 24/7 community team helping users deal with bad actors and any issue they have on our platform," he said.

items.title: No mandatory dating app ID checks as govt targets romance scams
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: There are no plans to introduce mandatory identity verification for dating app users, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching. Instead, she said the government was focusing on stronger platform safeguards, improved scam detection and greater public awareness to tackle online fraud. These included detection and removal of fraudulent accounts, impersonation attempts and coordinated scam networks; behavioural and technical measures to identify suspicious activities; accessible reporting mechanisms; timely enforcement action and preservation of information to support investigations.

items.title: Perkeso battles evolving fraud [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The number of company executives and doctors facing court action over false Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) claims highlights the growing complexity of fraud cases handled by the government agency. While cases have declined overall, Perkeso is seeing a worrying trend involving suspicious claims linked to government assistance programmes. Azman said some sophisticated fraud syndicates operated through networks involving employers, doctors and runners.

items.title: 'Sirens shouldn't override traffic rules,' say experts [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The rules governing the use of sirens and beacon lights by emergency vehicles and VIP escorts need a review to ensure traffic priority does not compromise public safety, experts said. Escort movements, they said, must also be made safer and more predictable for other road users, with standard procedures covering speed, lane changes, overtaking and intersections, while giving motorists enough time to react. Law said while sirens and beacons could indicate that emergency and escort vehicles had priority, drivers still had to follow standard road safety practices.

items.title: National Housing Policy: What does the policy mean for Malaysians
items.summary: The policy proposes using more detailed local data to determine where housing is needed, expanding rental and financing options, making better use of existing housing stock and strengthening the way housing projects are approved and delivered. Here is what the policy proposes and how it helps Malaysians with housing related matters. The DRN looks to ensure housing projections at the sub-district and district level, take into account existing housing supply, vacant units, housing types, household income and price categories.

items.title: Israel warns Hamas over kite launches from Gaza
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel warned Hamas on Sunday that it would step up operations in Gaza if launches of kites, drones and balloons towards Israel continued, after a recent increase in such incidents, while Hamas denied responsibility. The incidents have revived memories of waves of incendiary kites and balloons launched from Gaza in previous years, which sparked fires in agricultural lands in southern Israel. Hamas meanwhile denied responsibility for the launches.

items.title: Norwegian King Harald's health has 'deteriorated', palace says
items.summary: OSLO: The health of Norway's 89-year-old King Harald V, who is in hospital due to complications from a blood condition, has "deteriorated" over the weekend, a statement from the palace said on Sunday. "His Majesty the King's health deteriorated over the weekend," said the palace. The Verdens Gang newspaper reported that his wife, Queen Sonja, their son Crown Prince Haakon, who is acting as regent in Harald's absence, and Haakon's wife Crown Princess Mette-Marit visited him on Sunday, as did the King's sister.

items.title: Landslide at Guinea landfill kills 30
items.summary: CONAKRY: A landslide at a landfill in Guinea's capital killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted the collapse of a massive mound of waste that engulfed nearby tents and shacks. The landslide took place at around 2am (0200 GMT) in the Gbessia commune of Conakry, according to a government statement. The death toll was 30, with six people seriously injured and 16 more lightly injured, the statement said.

items.title: Trump takes starring role at Washington's IndyCar debut
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump rode a ceremonial lap in his armoured limousine and waved the green flag to start Sunday's IndyCar race through the streets of Washington, capping celebrations of America's 250th birthday. "It has turned out to be bigger than we ever thought possible," Trump told race telecaster Fox. This is incredible," Kirkwood said.

items.title: Tens of thousands ordered to evacuate in Nevada as fire threatens Reno
items.summary: About 42,000 residents have been displaced or are in active evacuation areas, with an additional 45,000 under a "be prepared to evacuate" status as the Hawk Fire threatened northern Reno, local officials said late Sunday morning. The fire has burned 13,000 acres (5,261 hectares) so far, officials said at a press conference on Sunday. The fire was human-caused and remains under investigation, they said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Syria, Israel hold US-mediated talks to ease tensions
items.summary: DAMASCUS: Syria and Israel held high-level, US-mediated talks in Jordan on Sunday aimed at easing tensions following recent Israeli strikes on Syrian territory, Syria's state news agency SANA reported, citing a diplomatic source at the foreign ministry. Talks had been suspended since the start of the Iran war, while Syria cut off contact entirely after Israeli strikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase last week, according to Shaibani. Syria and Israel have technically been at war since 1948.

items.title: Selangor, Putrajaya step up flood fight
items.summary: "Other measures include assessing the capacity of Batu Dam and Klang Gate Dam, identifying sites for new flood retention ponds, upgrading three ponds and coordinating river dredging and desilting works," the statement said. They will also identify suitable upstream locations for new flood retention ponds. The Selangor Irrigation and Drainage Department will identify three existing ponds for upgrading: Kampung Laksamana Pond, Sungai Kertas Pond and Bukit Lagong Pond.

items.title: Quake near Tokyo injures 37, disrupts train services
items.summary: TOKYO: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck near Tokyo early yesterday, injuring at least 37 people and disrupting travel in the megacity. The quake struck the southern part of the Ibaraki Prefecture near Tokyo at 2am, the Japan Meteorological Agency said. Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency said at least 37 people had suffered minor injuries.

items.title: 1,000 youths light up Kota Baru
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Nearly 1,000 youths, including 20 disabled people, took part in a 3km walk here on Saturday night to celebrate patriotism and unity ahead of National Day. The inaugural Madani Glow Walk brought together youths from various backgrounds, including tertiary students, to mark the celebrations. Nearly 500 participants registered within 10 days."

items.title: Rubber market to trade higher on strong demand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian rubber market is expected to trade higher this week, supported by strong demand and concerns over supply constraints. The Malaysian Rubber Glove Manufacturers Association (Margma) said demand is expected to strengthen, particularly in China, which has pledged additional fiscal policy measures aimed at supporting economic growth. Industry expert Denis Low said the Malaysian rubber market is expected to trend slightly higher next week, supported by potential restocking demand from China and firmer crude oil prices.

items.title: Tanah Merah depot escapees identifiable by bright green uniforms, shaved heads
items.summary: "Their last known location was Bukit Tebu, Tanah Merah. The statement posted on the Kelantan contingent police headquarters' Facebook page said the fugitives comprise seven Thai nationals, one Indonesian, one Bangladeshi and one Rohingya. Information can be directed to the Tanah Merah District Control Centre at 09-955 6222 (district police headquarters), 09-955 6223 (Tanah Merah police station), or via WhatsApp at 011-2955 5518.

items.title: Amirudin denies fake poster on Selangor's Sukma holiday
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has denied a viral poster claiming a special public holiday will be declared following the state's 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma) victory. Amirudin said any official announcement would be made during the Sukma closing ceremony on Aug 24 at Aneka Walk, Section 14. Earlier, state Youth, Sports, and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi said the state government would consider declaring a special public holiday if Selangor won the overall title.

items.title: China tax crackdown forcing wealthy investors to assess offshore trusts
items.summary: A growing campaign to tax offshore wealth is forcing wealthy Chinese people to rethink their trust structures and investment holdings, lawyers and advisers say, as Beijing sharpens its focus on capital outflows and rule enforcement amid growing fiscal strains. In late July, authorities overhauled rules to impose a 20 per cent income tax on offshore trusts, while tax offices in major cities like Beijing and Hangzhou have started to enforce taxation on returns from offshore insurance policies. Offshore trusts have gained popularity in recent years as a growing number of Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong.

items.title: Energy crisis just getting started
items.summary: The Iran war has pushed the global oil refining industry to the brink, signalling that diesel and petrol prices may remain elevated for years. The divergence between crude and fuel prices tells the story. Benchmark Brent crude oil is currently around US$90 a barrel.

items.title: 'We have faced this many times': Pas ready for action over Hadi's article
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas is ready to face any action by the authorities following a police investigation into an article written by its president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang. Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said it was normal for party leaders, including the president, to be called up by police following reports lodged over their statements or writings. Syahir, who is also Pas assistant secretary-general, said police launched an investigation into Hadi following reports lodged by DAP supporters.

items.title: #NSTviral: Woman finds banknotes with rust stains after 2 years in money box [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KUALA LUMPUR: A woman was shocked to find several banknotes stored in a money box damaged and covered in rust stains after her home was flooded about two years ago. She said the money box had been left on the floor when floodwaters entered her home two years ago, but she only discovered the damage when she opened it recently to deposit her children's savings at a bank. One user, @Duniahanyapinjamanshop, said she had previously managed to exchange banknotes that had been damaged by termites.

items.title: MSF condemns Israel's closure of probes into attacks killing 4 staff
items.summary: GENEVA: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has condemned the Israeli authorities' decision to close two cases referred by the organisation for review without opening criminal investigations, the Palestine News and Info Agency (WAFA) reported. The two cases concern multiple attacks on an MSF convoy in Gaza City in November 2023, which killed two people, and an airstrike on an MSF shelter in Khan Younis in February 2024, which killed two people and injured six others. MSF said its staff members and their family members had been killed by Israeli forces despite the organisation having notified Israeli authorities of their locations.

items.title: One of two men nabbed by Thai cops also on Kelantan police's wanted list
items.summary: KOTA BARU: One of the two Malaysians arrested by Thai police recently for possessing 1,560 Epam pills is on Kelantan police's wanted list. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said checks found that both men had records for narcotics-related offences in Malaysia, namely drug-trafficking and drug possession. Meanwhile, Yusoff said state police would tomorrow dispose of 6,536 items of drug evidence worth RM1.1 million from cases investigated between 2008 and 2024.

items.title: Over RM720 mil spent on welfare aid for seniors, PwD, chronic patients - Nancy
items.summary: KUCHING: The Social Welfare Department has spent about RM728.5 million to support the welfare of senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PwD) and chronic patients nationwide as of June this year. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the allocation was channelled through the Senior Citizen Assistance (BWE) and the Assistance for Care of Bedridden Persons with Disabilities and Bedridden Chronic Patients (BPT). "To ease the burden on families, the Social Welfare Department also assists with the care of bedridden persons with disabilities, bedridden chronic patients and non-bedridden chronic patients who meet the eligibility criteria.

items.title: Bersatu leaders accuse Pas of pre-empting ROS on supreme council quorum issue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu leaders today accused Pas, which leads Perikatan Nasional (PN), of pre-empting the Registrar of Societies (ROS) over claims that Bersatu no longer has the quorum to hold meetings of its Supreme Leadership Council. Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said that, to date, ROS itself had never issued any statement questioning Bersatu's legitimacy or announced that the party had been dissolved. Tun Faisal said the matter of quorum was clearly provided for under the Bersatu Constitution, with Clause 13.12 stating that the quorum for a supreme council meeting was half of the total number of council members.

items.title: Communities celebrate National Month through arts, cultural heritage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The spirit of the National Month is expressed not only by flying the Jalur Gemilang but also through appreciation of cultural heritage and creative arts among the community. She said her participation in the event also gave her children an opportunity to see first-hand efforts to promote cultural heritage in the spirit of the National Day celebrations. Normaizan said her participation in the programme also encouraged her third child, Asfa Nur Nelydhia Hasmisham, 11, to take part in the independence-themed traditional attire competition.

items.title: Two boys, 13 and 16, found dead after being swept away by strong currents in Sabah
items.summary: KENINGAU, Aug 23 — Two teenage boys who were reported missing after being swept away by strong currents in Sungai Pegalan, Kampung Bakti here yesterday, were found dead today. The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Centre said the body of the first victim, Jasti Gomen, 16, was found at 10.34am, while the second victim, Khend Rommel Ponce Caceres, 13, was found at 3.55pm. “The body of the first victim was found by the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) 50 metres from the place he was reported to have been swept away, while the second victim was found 80 metres away,” the Sabah JBPM said in a statement today.

items.title: No militants have crossed into Malaysia after southern Thailand attacks, authorities say
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Aug 23 — There has been no reported attempt by militants or guerrillas from Southern Thailand to cross into Kelantan so far, following last night’s coordinated bombings and violent attacks across three southern Thai provinces. Confirming this, Southeast Brigade Commander of the General Operations Force (PGA) SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said border security along the Malaysia-Thailand frontier is being tightened as a precaution, with front-line personnel on high alert for any potential infiltration attempts. Meanwhile, Mohd Yusoff confirmed today that no Malaysians were caught in last night’s bombings and violence across three southern Thai provinces.

items.title: October Sarawak assembly sitting no sign of November state election, says Abdul Karim
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 23 — The possibility of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting being brought forward to October is not an indication that the next state election will be held in November, said Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah. He said the DUN normally sits at least twice a year, and therefore the possible change from November to October should not be linked to speculation over the timing of the state election. Usually, the sitting is held in November.

items.title: Care should not fall on families alone, says Nancy as welfare spending hits RM728m
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 23 — The Social Welfare Department (JKM) has spent about RM728.5 million to support the welfare of senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PwD) and chronic patients nationwide as of June this year. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the allocation was channelled through the Senior Citizen Assistance (BWE) and the Assistance for Care of Bedridden Persons with Disabilities and Bedridden Chronic Patients (BPT). “To ease the burden on families, the Social Welfare Department also assists with the care of bedridden persons with disabilities, bedridden chronic patients and non-bedridden chronic patients who meet the eligibility criteria.

items.title: Kemaman police detain man over alleged seditious Facebook post against Royal Institution and govt
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 23 — Police have detained a man suspected of making a seditious and insulting Facebook post against the Royal Institution, the Malaysian government and a security agency. Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the 39-year-old man was arrested in Damansara Damai, Petaling Jaya, Selangor on Wednesday, and a mobile phone and two SIM cards were seized. Mohd Razi said the man has been remanded until Wednesday to assist in the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

items.title: Haze watch: Sungai Petani, Johan Setia worsen as five more areas in Malaysia edge towards unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — The haze picture shifted across peninsular Malaysia this afternoon, with Sungai Petani worsening and five other areas creeping towards unhealthy levels, while Sarawak remained the country’s worst-affected region. Creeping towards unhealthy Five locations were now hovering close to the unhealthy threshold, with Klang recording 95, Banting and Putrajaya 93 each, Bukit Rambai in Melaka 92 and Nilai in Negeri Sembilan 91. All five remained in the moderate category but were within 10 points of the unhealthy threshold.

items.title: Terengganu’s Teluk Kalong Beach hit by coal pollution again, second incident this year
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 23 — Teluk Kalong Beach here has once again been affected by coal pollution over the past three days, believed to have originated from a barge that broke apart near the beach last January. He said the beach had experienced similar pollution last January following a coal spill from a barge, although cleanup operations were subsequently carried out by the parties involved. “I hope the authorities will immediately carry out cleanup operations to remove the coal debris, ensuring the cleanliness of the beach as well as the safety and well-being of fishermen and visitors,” he told Bernama when met at Teluk Kalong Beach today.

items.title: Zahid: Malaysia should build full ecosystem to lead global Muslim travel economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Malaysia must move beyond being the world’s leading Muslim-friendly destination and become a global hub for the Muslim travel economy, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said the country should build an ecosystem that connects tourism with halal innovation, trade, technology and local enterprises, while creating opportunities for entrepreneurs, small businesses and communities. Tourism should therefore be viewed as an economic multiplier,” he said.

items.title: MCMC, Selangor to expand filtered internet service to public premises and private institutions, says exco
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 23 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with the Selangor state government, plans to expand its filtered internet service to public premises and private higher learning institutions (IPTS). He said content filtering was important to ensure digital access was not misused during important activities such as prayers and learning sessions. On cyber threats, Mohammad Fahmi said 35,073 online scam cases were recorded as of June, involving losses of RM951.7 million, with investment scams accounting for RM413.8 million.

items.title: Selangor may declare holiday if host contingent emerge overall Sukma champions, says exco
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 23 — The Selangor government will consider declaring an occasional holiday if the host contingent emerge overall champions at the ongoing Malaysia Games (SUKMA) 2026. State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi said the matter would only be announced after the medal tally is finalised, with the Selangor contingent looking well placed to end the Games on a high. Najwan said that as of 2.50 pm today, Selangor had collected 85 gold medals, with the latest contributed by, among others, the women’s Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) esports team, women’s 3m springboard diving, women’s singles table tennis and men’s singles lawn bowls.

items.title: Got 20,000 tech engineers, but where are the investors? Jerejak may have the answer, says Bayan Baru MP
items.summary: Bayan Baru MP Sim Tze Tzin said the proposed 32-hectare development could bring venture capitalists, private equity firms, bankers and technology investors closer to the engineers driving Penang’s semiconductor industry, The Star reported. Sim said Penang has about 20,000 integrated circuit design engineers, many of whom remain salaried employees because they lack investors to help them establish their own companies. Sim, who lived in Silicon Valley for six years, said regular interaction between engineers, entrepreneurs and investors could help generate new ideas and spur the growth of Penang’s technology sector.

items.title: PM approves additional RM1m for Hindu crematorium project in Bagan, says PHEB
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Aug 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM1 million allocation to the Penang State Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) for the construction of a modern Hindu crematorium in Bagan here, said PHEB chairman RSN Rayer. He said the additional allocation brought the total funding for the project to RM2.5 million, up from the RM1.5 million previously approved by Anwar. He said the original RM1.5 million allocation was found to be insufficient to implement the project, which is much needed by the Hindu community, particularly in Seberang Perai.

items.title: Post-mortem shows 11-year-old tahfiz participant found in Lenggeng pond died from drowning, police say no signs of abuse
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 23 — An 11-year-old boy who was found in a pond near a foundation centre in Kampung Kapal, Lenggeng early today died from drowning, resulting in a lack of oxygen, police said. “External and internal examinations of the victim’s body also found no other injuries or signs indicating abuse,” the senior police officer was quoted as saying. The boy had been reported missing while taking part in a tahfiz – a Quran memorisation – programme before he was found in a weak condition in a pond near the site.

items.title: After southern Thailand blasts, Wisma Putra tells Malaysians to think twice before crossing border
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Malaysians planning to travel to or cross into southern Thailand have been urged to exercise heightened caution and postpone non-essential trips following a wave of bomb blasts and other attacks across the region last night. The Foreign Ministry, also called Wisma Putra, said no Malaysians had been reported affected by the incidents in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, but advised those residing in, travelling through or planning trips to the affected areas to remain vigilant and follow local security instructions. “Malaysians residing in, travelling through, or intending to travel to and from the southern border provinces of Thailand are strongly advised to exercise heightened caution, remain vigilant, and strictly observe all safety advisories, curfews, and security instructions implemented by local authorities,” it said in a media advisory today.

items.title: IIUM ends ties with academic behind controversial Roman-Malay shipbuilding claim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) has confirmed that controversial academic Solehah Yaacob is no longer with the university, months after she drew public scrutiny over claims that ancient Romans learned shipbuilding from Malays and that meteor activity may explain Kedah’s iron ore deposits. The university said Solehah was also barred from using any official title, position or affiliation linking her to IIUM in promotional materials, media reports, publications, advertisements, social media content, publicity materials or other forms of public dissemination. IIUM said the clarification was necessary to prevent confusion over Solehah’s status and protect the university’s institutional integrity in academic representation.

items.title: Sabah searchers find body of one boy after two teens swept away in Keningau river
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 23 — A recreational outing turned tragic when a 16-year-old boy was found dead in Sungai Pegalan, Keningau today, while rescuers continue searching for his 13-year-old friend who was swept away by the strong current. Family members alerted police after learning that the boys were missing, prompting a search and rescue operation. A joint search and rescue team comprising seven police officers, nine firefighters and 13 APM personnel remains deployed at the scene in the search for Khend.

items.title: Health Ministry reports surge in respiratory illnesses as several areas hit unhealthy API levels
items.summary: “URTI recorded the highest number at 3,674 cases, an increase from 1,637, while asthma cases reached 219 compared with 61 cases. Conjunctivitis cases, meanwhile, dropped to 146 from 157 cases,” he said. On heat-related illnesses, Dzulkefly said 90 cases had been recorded, comprising 71 cases of heat exhaustion, 14 heatstroke cases and five heat cramps cases.

items.title: Neighbourly row lands 80-year-old man in Penang Hospital, 62-year-old man in police custody
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 23 — A dispute between neighbours turned violent this morning when a 62-year-old man allegedly attacked his 80-year-old neighbour with a steel rod in Jalan Perak here. George Town district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received information about the incident at about 9.55am, with preliminary investigations indicating the assault happened about 9.30am outside the victim’s house, The Star reported. “The victim, an 80-year-old local man, was allegedly assaulted by his 62-year-old neighbour, who used a steel rod,” he was quoted as saying.

items.title: Police launch lockdown operation after ten migrants escape Tanah Merah Immigration Depot
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 23 — Ten undocumented migrants escaped from the Tanah Merah Immigration Depot early this morning, police said. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said all the migrants were under the custody of the Kelantan Immigration Department and that police would conduct further investigations into the incident. We will investigate further,” he told a press conference at the Kelantan police contingent headquarters here.

items.title: BN conducting detailed study before deciding on Melaka election cooperation, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is conducting a detailed study on the possibility of cooperating with any political coalition in the upcoming Melaka state election, said its chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said any decision on the matter would be made by the Melaka BN leadership and finalised at the central level. In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional two.

items.title: Forensic audit needed to determine abuse or governance lapses in Felda, says DPM Zahid
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said a management audit alone would be insufficient, given that issues involving the agency had persisted for a long time and resulted in losses amounting to billions of ringgit. “Felda is facing very serious and long-standing problems. Last Friday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would await the full report of the Special Task Force investigating Felda’s management issues before making any official announcement.

items.title: GOF seizes RM1.135m in gold‑mining equipment in Kuala Betis raid; suspect allegedly misused sand‑extraction permit
items.summary: GUA MUSANG, Aug 23 — The General Operations Force (GOF) seized equipment worth RM1.135 million believed to have been used for illegal gold mining and arrested four men, including a Chinese national, in a raid at the Kuala Betis Resettlement Scheme (RPS) here yesterday. Southeast Brigade commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid, conducted at about 4pm, was carried out by the brigade’s intelligence team under Ops Gali Mega (Eastern Zone). He said checks at the site uncovered two excavators, sluice boxes, suction machines, generator sets each, 51 pieces of grass carpet in various sizes and three rolls of grass carpet, all believed to have been used in the gold mining operation.

items.title: Teen girl fled motorcyclist after he allegedly told her to undress, Kelantan police now investigating possible sexual assault
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 23 — Police are looking into a possible sexual offence involving a 15-year-old girl who was found unconscious by the roadside in Machang on August 20, after she allegedly fled from a man who told her to remove her clothes. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the girl had run away from home before meeting the unidentified motorcyclist and accepting a ride from him, Harian Metro reported today. Mohd Yusoff said a medical examination found no evidence of rape, but police were concerned that an attempted sexual offence may have occurred.

items.title: No Malaysians affected by simultaneous attacks in three southern Thai provinces, says Kelantan police chief
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 23 — Kelantan Police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said there is no report of Malaysians being affected by a series of simultaneous violent incidents in three provinces in southern Thailand last night. He said the advice was not new and had been conveyed several times to Malaysians planning to travel to southern Thailand. “I advised them not to enter Hat Yai as there were 51 incidents in three provinces in southern Thailand last night,” he said.

items.title: Man dies after motorcycle hits fallen tree on Kuala Terengganu–Kota Bharu road in Setiu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — A permanent resident Indonesian man died after his motorcycle crashed into a fallen tree along Jalan Kampung Merang on the Kuala Terengganu–Kota Bharu coastal route late last night. Bernama reported that the victim, identified as 68‑year‑old construction worker Darman Khamis, was believed to be travelling from Kuala Terengganu towards Kampung Bari Besar when the crash occurred. Setiu district police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the accident at about 12.10am from the Setiu district police traffic complaint counter.

items.title: Predawn robbery at Miri mini market leaves worker with injuries, police nab three Malaysian suspects
items.summary: MIRI, Aug 23 — A quiet early morning at a Tudan mini-market turned violent when three men allegedly broke into the premises, attacked an employee and fled with cash and other items. “The victim suffered injuries to her hand and shoulder before receiving treatment at Miri Hospital,” Miri district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah was quoted as saying. Police later arrested three Malaysian men aged between 28 and 39, acting on information received and conducting follow-up investigations.

items.title: Schools in 10 Sarawak districts to resume classes tomorrow as API improves
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 23 — All primary and secondary schools under the 10 District Education Offices (PPDs) in Sarawak will operate as usual from tomorrow, following improvements in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. The Sarawak State Education Department (JPNS) said the schools under the PPDs of Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu and Betong would reopen as scheduled. JPNS reminded schools to take precautionary measures if haze affects their respective areas.

items.title: EMGS: International students generate RM20b a year for Malaysia’s economy, each contributing an estimated RM10,000 monthly
items.summary: KUALA NERUS, Aug 23 — The presence of about 167,000 international students in Malaysia currently contributes around RM20 billion annually to the country’s economy through spending on tuition fees and living expenses, said Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) chief executive officer (CEO) Novie Tajuddin. He said Malaysia aims to attract 500,000 international students by 2035, as outlined in the 10-year Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint. “We currently have 167,000 international students.

items.title: Allegedly struck with shoe and pencil case: Penang Education Dept steps in after 12-year-old cries assault by teacher in class
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 23 — The Penang Education Department has taken precautionary steps to protect a 12-year-old boy while investigating a complaint that he was allegedly assaulted by a teacher at a school in the Northeast district. The department said the teacher no longer has direct contact with the pupil, who has also been referred to the school’s Guidance and Counselling teacher for appropriate support and intervention, Harian Metro reported today. He said the Northeast Penang District Education Office was conducting the investigation and would take further action based on its findings.
